newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PLDT sets Manila's first Internet backbone.
newsitem.headline: PLDT sets Manila's first Internet backbone.

text.p: The Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co said it has started to operate the country's first Internet hub.

"The introduction of our very own network access point, to be called the Philippine Internet Exchange, shall localise the exchange of Internet traffic within the Philippines," said PLDT first vice-president Cesar Reyes at the launching late Thursday.
Reyes said the exchange eliminates the need to route local information to the host servers located overseas and reduces the cost for the country's Internet service providers (ISPs).

Reyes said PLDT has signed agreements with the country's five largest ISPs namely Infocom Technologies Inc, Mosaic Communications, IPHIL Communications Network Inc, Virtualink International Corp and WorldTel Philippines Inc.
Reyes said PLDT and the five ISPs will share the cost of setting up the $600,000 Internet exchange.
PLDT owns 51 percent of Infocom Technologies. At present, the country has over 120 Internet providers.
